rule: A new row needs a page dated 2025–2026 that names it and carries a copied sentence (scripts/library-check.cjs), then a map check: ok only when the map shows the place at that address, not closed, with a review dated within the last six months. Google Maps barely covers mainland China, so each place was checked on Baidu Maps (map.baidu.com, no sign-in; Amap asks for a Chinese phone number to sign in, so it was not used). A place no map could find at the page's address was left out.
agents: four Haiku agents (sit-down restaurants · quick bites and cafés · children and rainy days · landmarks), five web searches each; 44 rows offered, 39 passed library-check.cjs, 16 went in

estimates: The things-to-do format requires ages, hours, indoors and pram for every row. They are read from each page's description where it says so; otherwise they are the reviewer's estimate. No price, opening hour or age band was written that a page did not show, except the Monday closings, which Baidu Maps lists.

recheck_of_older_rows.rule: A row gets ok only from a current listing, its own site or recent reviews with nothing saying closed (docs/EATS.md). A row is taken out when a search could not find the place at all or the sources disagree; a place found but not freshly confirmed stays without ok.
recheck_of_older_rows.scope: the 3 rows without ok; nothing else in the town was re-checked
recheck_of_older_rows.how: Google Maps opened in headless Chromium (2026-11-23), limited view without a reviews tab, so no review date could be read; each row searched with its Chinese name (zh) and/or its English name and the town. Maps' coverage of mainland China is thin: many listings carry no hours at all. A list result's hours line ('Open · Closes 10 PM', or 'Open now', which Maps shows only when it holds the place's hours) counted as a current listing. Where Maps could not settle a row, one web search (snippets only, pages not opened) was made for it.
